name: Point of imitation
description: one voice states a motif, the others enter with the same motif at staggered distances, usually a fourth or fifth apart. Each section of text gets its own point. This is the *form*, not a device: a piece is a chain of them.

name: Stepwise motion, overwhelmingly
description: real Palestrina is around 80% stepwise. A leap is an event. Any line that arpeggiates is out of style.

name: A leap answered by a step in the opposite direction
description: the rule that makes the lines singable. After a leap of a fourth or more, the next note steps back inside it. Never two leaps in the same direction.

name: The arch
description: a voice rises to a single high point and descends. One peak per phrase, and the peak is not repeated.

name: Suspension and resolution
description: a voice holds while the harmony changes beneath it, creating a dissonance on the strong beat, then falls by step: `G4h~ G4q F4q`. The engine of Renaissance expression, and the only place dissonance is allowed on a strong beat.

name: Passing dissonance on the weak beat
description: the other permitted dissonance, and only when approached and left by step.

name: Cambiata
description: the one licensed "wrong" figure: down a step, down a third, up a step, up a step. A formula worth having in the vocabulary because it sounds authentic and nothing else does the same job.

name: Cadence with a suspended fourth
description: the standard close: the upper voice suspends over the penultimate bass note, resolves down, and the final is reached by step. The leading tone rises.

name: Voice pairing
description: two voices move together in thirds or sixths, answered by the other two. Gives contrast without changing the number of parts.

name: Reduced scoring
description: dropping from five voices to two or three for a phrase, then returning to full. The Renaissance equivalent of a dynamic change, and the principal means of shaping a piece.

name: Homophony for emphasis
description: all voices in the same rhythm on one phrase of text, usually a short one, then back to polyphony. Rare and therefore striking.

name: Rests as entries
description: a voice is silent for several bars before its next point of imitation. Voices enter and drop out constantly, and a texture where all voices sing continuously is a texture with no articulation.

name: Alberti bass
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Murky bass (octave alternation)
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Waltz bass (3/4, L:1/8)
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Point of imitation
description: a motif stated by one voice and answered by the others at staggered entries, usually a fourth or fifth apart. Each phrase of text gets its own, and the next point begins before the previous one has finished. That overlap is the technique.

name: Overlapping cadences
description: as one voice reaches its cadence, another begins the next point. A cadence where every voice stops together is an ending, and there should be very few.

name: Reduced scoring
description: dropping from five voices to two or three for a phrase, then returning. The principal means of shaping, and this repertoire's equivalent of a dynamic change.

name: Voice pairing
description: two voices in thirds or sixths answered by the other two. Contrast without changing the number of parts.

name: Homophonic declamation
description: all voices in the rhythm of the words for one short phrase. Used for the most important line of text, and its rarity is what makes it land.

name: Full-texture climax
description: all voices sounding together for the first time, placed late.

name: Suspension and resolution
description: a voice holds while the bass moves, creating a strong-beat dissonance, then falls by step. The only licensed strong-beat dissonance, and the engine of the expression.

name: Suspension chain
description: several in succession, the resolution of one preparing the next.

name: Passing dissonance on a weak beat
description: approached and left by step. The other permitted dissonance.

name: Cambiata
description: down a step, down a third, up a step, up a step. The one licensed irregular figure and it sounds unmistakably of the period.

name: Portamento / anticipation
description: the cadential note arrived at early as a short note before the beat.

name: Inversion of the motif
description: the same shape upside down, used for a later entry so the point of imitation stays fresh.

name: Augmentation
description: of the motif in the lowest voice for a final statement.

name: The arch
description: one high point per phrase, approached and left by step. The peak is not repeated.

name: Leap answered by step in the opposite direction
description: after any leap of a fourth or more, the line steps back inside it.

name: Stepwise motion overwhelmingly
description: around 80% of intervals. A leap is an event.

name: The clivis at a cadence
description: the standard cadential formula: the upper voice suspends over the penultimate bass, resolves down, and the leading tone rises to the final.

name: Triads in root position and first inversion
description: the whole vocabulary. No seventh chords except as suspensions.

name: Musica ficta
description: the leading tone raised at cadences, and B-flat used to avoid a tritone against F. The only chromaticism in the style.

name: Plagal cadence for a final Amen
description: IV to I, all voices, extended.

name: Modal rather than tonal
description: the piece is in a mode, and the cadence points are the mode's own degrees, not a tonic-dominant axis.

name: Point of imitation
description: as in Palestrina, and the default in the earlier madrigal texture: a motif passed between voices at staggered entries.

name: The declaiming solo over a slow bass
description: one voice in speech rhythm, the bass holding whole notes underneath: `C3w` under a freely-moving upper line. The recitative texture, and Monteverdi's invention as a musical form.

name: Basso continuo in slow harmonic rhythm
description: `G2w`, `C3w`, one chord per bar or per two bars. It supports; it does not compete.

name: Descending tetrachord ground
description: `A3h G3h F3h E3h` repeated as an ostinato under changing upper material. The lament bass, and the *Lamento della Ninfa* is built entirely on one. The most reusable device in his vocabulary.

name: Stile concitato
description: the "agitated style": rapid repeated notes on one pitch, `C4s ×16`, representing warfare and passion. Monteverdi's own invention and unmistakably his.

name: Unprepared dissonance for a word
description: a seventh or a ninth entered without preparation because the text says *cruda*, *dolore*, *morte*. Forbidden in the *prima pratica* and the whole point of the second.

name: Suspension chains
description: as in Palestrina, but longer and more insistent, and allowed to resolve onto another dissonance.

name: Homophonic declamation
description: all voices together in the rhythm of the words, for a line of text that must be understood. Alternates with polyphony.

name: Voice pairs answering
description: two upper voices against two lower, trading a phrase. The concertato texture.

name: Chromatic descent in the bass
description: semitone by semitone, `A2q Ab2q G2q Gb2q`. Grief. Later than Palestrina and earlier than everyone else who used it.

name: Echo
description: a phrase repeated immediately, quieter, often by a different voice or at a distance. Written as a literal repeat.

name: Silence for a word
description: everything stops before a crucial word. The most Monteverdian gesture there is, and it costs one rest.

name: Rising line for rising text
description: *ascende*, *cielo*, *alto*. Literal and deliberate.

name: Falling chromatic line for grief
description: *dolore*, *morte*, *pianto*. Usually a descending fourth by semitones.

name: The written sigh
description: a rest inside a word, then a falling second. *Sospiro* painted by an actual gap.

name: Fast imitative scattering for flight
description: *fugge*, *vola*: the voices chase each other in close entries.

name: Stillness for stillness
description: a held chord, all voices, no motion, for *silenzio* or *dorme*.

name: Silence before the crucial word
description: everything stops, then the word arrives alone. The most Monteverdian gesture there is and it costs one rest.

name: Sudden homophony for a line that must be understood
description: all voices in the rhythm of speech, then back to polyphony.

name: Unprepared dissonance
description: a seventh or ninth entered without preparation because the text demands it. Forbidden in the older practice; the entire point of the newer one.

name: Cross relation
description: the same pitch class natural in one voice and altered in another, close together. Harsh and intentional.

name: The descending tetrachord ground
description: `A3 G3 F3 E3` repeated as an ostinato under changing upper material. The lament bass; the *Lamento della Ninfa* is built entirely on one, and it is the most reusable device in his vocabulary.

name: Slow harmonic rhythm under recitative
description: one chord for a bar or two while the voice declaims freely above it.

name: Chromatic bass descent
description: semitone by semitone, for grief.

name: The unresolved suspension
description: a dissonance resolving onto another dissonance rather than a consonance.

name: Modal harmony with expressive ficta
description: the raised leading tone used for intensity rather than only at cadences.

name: Stile concitato
description: the "agitated style": rapid repeated notes on one pitch, `C4s ×16`, for warfare and passion. His own invention and unmistakable.

name: Speech rhythm
description: the vocal line following the accentuation of the words, not the barline. Long notes on stressed syllables, short runs on unstressed.

name: Echo
description: a phrase repeated immediately, quieter, often by a different voice or at a distance.

name: Concertato contrast
description: a small group answered by a large one, or voices answered by instruments. The Baroque's founding textural idea.

name: The ritornello
description: a short instrumental refrain between vocal sections.

name: Ornamental division on a long note
description: the voice decorating a held pitch with rapid written-out figuration.

name: Strophic variation
description: the same bass and harmonic plan, new melody in each verse. Between strict strophic and through-composed.

name: Recitative — aria alternation
description: declamation for narrative, lyrical measured writing for reflection. The structural invention that makes opera possible.

name: A phrase length set by the line of text
description: not by four-bar symmetry.
